# Go Switch `opencode-go-switch` keeps an OpenCode Go session running: it stays on the account that still has headroom and moves to the next account inside the same request when a limit hits. It is a plugin for OpenCode and an extension for [Pi](https://pi.dev), in one package; install it in either or both. The rules below are the same in both, and [Pi](#pi) lists what differs there. [![CI workflow status](https://github.com/xonika9/opencode-go-switch/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/xonika9/opencode-go-switch/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/opencode-go-switch)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/opencode-go-switch) [![License](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/opencode-go-switch)](LICENSE) ## Why OpenCode Go meters usage in three windows: a rolling 5-hour window, a weekly window, and a monthly window. With one subscription, a window eventually runs out mid-session. With several subscriptions you can keep working, but every switch drops the provider's prompt cache, so the next request starts colder. So the plugin switches only when it has to. It keeps the account you are already using while that account has known headroom or its usage is unknown, and it goes looking for another account only when the current one can no longer serve a request. A recovered account does not pull the current account away: the current one stays until it fails. ## How it decides - **Eligible** means usage is known for all three windows, none of them is exhausted, the key is not marked invalid, the account is not disabled, and it is not cooling down after an unexplained limit. Anything else is not eligible. - **Sticky while usable.** The current account stays current while it is eligible, and also while its usage is unknown and requests keep succeeding. Unknown usage is not treated as a reason to move; a failing response is. - **Forced switch order.** Eligible accounts come first, ordered by the earliest monthly reset. Next come eligible accounts without a usable monthly reset (none reported, or already in the past), then accounts whose usage is unknown. Ties break by label, then by id. Exhausted, cooling-down, disabled, and invalid-key accounts are never candidates. - **One request, one provider.** A switch re-sends the same request, with the same URL, body, model, and provider, under the next account's key. Redirects are not followed on that retry; a redirect response is handed back to OpenCode as it is. - **Nothing left means the original error.** When no account can carry the request, OpenCode receives the provider's original response, unchanged. ## Provider responses The plugin only reacts to the provider response for the `opencode-go` provider (or whichever `providerID` you configure): | Response | What usage says | What the plugin does | | --- | --- | --- | | `429` or `402` | A fresh read shows no window flagged as limited | Leaves the response alone: this limit did not come from a Go window. | | `429` or `402` | A fresh read confirms an exhausted window | Marks the account exhausted, switches, and retries with the next account. | | `429` or `402` | Usage cannot be read (timeout, network error, HTTP error, odd shape), or a window is still flagged as limited after its reset time | Sets the account aside until `Retry-After`, or `fallbackCooldownMs` when the header is missing, switches, and retries. A later successful usage read does not end that cooldown early. | | `401` | Either | Marks the key invalid, switches, and retries. | | `403` | Either | Returns the response unchanged: no switch, no state change. | | Any other status | Either | Returns the response unchanged. | The retry loop repeats while responses are `429`, `402`, or `401` and an untried account remains. OpenCode has its own retry for failed requests. The plugin declines it (`retry: false`) only for `429` and `402` when there is at least one account and every account is out for a confirmed reason: an exhausted window, an invalid key, or a disabled connection. Retrying would just hit the same wall. In every other case the decision is left alone, including when an account is merely cooling down or has unknown usage, because OpenCode's retry may still succeed. ## What you see Every switch marks the chosen credential active in OpenCode (best effort; a rejected activation does not stop the request) and, when the client supports plugin notifications, sends a toast through OpenCode's terminal UI: ```text Now using

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and releases after `1.0.1` use calendar versions (see [Versioning](https://github.com/xonika9/opencode-go-switch/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#versioning)); earlier ones use semantic versions.

## Unreleased

## 26.11.2201 - 2026-11-22

### Added

- Pi extension in the same package (`pi install npm:opencode-go-switch`): switches OpenCode Go accounts inside the same request in Pi, with extra login slots for further accounts, the `/go-accounts` command, and the `go_accounts` tool.

### Changed

- Releases use calendar versions from here on. The number says nothing about compatibility, and a range such as `^1.0.1` does not include it. Nothing changes for an existing OpenCode setup.

### Fixed

- A request that authenticates with `x-goog-api-key` (Go models on the Google protocol) now carries the chosen account's key there, including on the retry, instead of keeping the previous key next to a new bearer header.

## 1.0.1 - 2026-11-18

### Changed

- When the usage endpoint stops answering during a limit, only the first account in a request waits out the two-second usage budget; later accounts in the same request go straight to the cooldown, so three limited accounts cost about two seconds instead of six.

## 1.0.0 - 2026-11-18

First release.

- Stays on the current OpenCode Go account while it has headroom in the 5-hour, weekly, and monthly windows, so ordinary requests keep the provider prompt cache.
- When that account runs out, switches to the next eligible account inside the same request and re-sends it with the new key; eligible accounts are ordered by earliest monthly reset, then those without a usable reset, then unknown usage.
- Reads usage from the Go usage endpoint and falls back to the provider's own limits: a `429`/`402` that fresh usage does not explain is left alone, and an unreadable limit, or a window still flagged after its reset time, sets the account aside for `Retry-After` or `fallbackCooldownMs`, and a later successful usage read does not shorten that.
- Marks a `401` as an invalid key, leaves `403` untouched, and declines OpenCode's retry only when every account is confirmed unusable.
- Remembers the current account across restarts, marks the active credential on every switch, and shows a toast in the terminal UI.
- Adds the `go_accounts` tool for status and explicit selection, with refusals for accounts that cannot serve a request.
- Keeps keys in OpenCode's credential store and in memory only; keys are never logged, stored, or returned, and there is no telemetry.
